properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 29 at 9:16AM EDT until October 30 at 8:00AM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor and Deland affecting Lake and Volusia
Counties.

.Persistent northeast winds and downstream tidal effects on the St
John River are slowing flow at Astor, which is also impacting river
levels upstream.

For the St. Johns River...including Deland, Astor...Minor to Moderate
flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and forecast to continue.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Deland.

* WHEN...Until Friday morning.

* IMPACTS...At 4.0 feet, Docks and piers are completely submerged at
Pier 44 Marina. Many docks are partially submerged at Hontoon
Landing Marina.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 AM EDT Thursday the stage was 4.0 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 3.5 feet.
- Forecast...At Deland, the river has reached a crest of 4.0 feet,
and is expected to begin a slow decline in Action Stage through
early next week.
- Flood stage is 4.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued late tonight at 1215 AM EDT.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 29 at 9:16AM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor and Deland affecting Lake and Volusia
Counties.

.Persistent northeast winds and downstream tidal effects on the St
John River are slowing flow at Astor, which is also impacting river
levels upstream.

For the St. Johns River...including Deland, Astor...Minor to Moderate
flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and forecast to continue.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 3.5 feet, Canals have overflowed into yards. Homes on
or near Wildhog, Bonnet and Snail roads become inaccessible with
several inches of water inside homes along the river and canals.
Docks at Astor Bridge marina and throughout Astor are completely
submerged. Bartram Rd and Holiday Circle are inaccessible with
yards completely submerged. Clair Street is inaccessible. Roads
flooded in South Moon Fish Camp, docks and yards at condominiums on
Juno Trail and water breaches the sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 AM EDT Thursday the stage was 3.7 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:30 AM EDT Thursday was 3.8 feet.
- Forecast...At Astor, river levels are forecast to slowly decline
but remain in Moderate Flood Stage for at least the next couple
weeks. Additional rises are possible as onshore winds
periodically increase.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 29 at 3:40PM MDT until October 29 at 6:30PM MDT by NWS El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa NM
properties.description:
FFWEPZ

The National Weather Service in El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Northeastern El Paso County in western Texas...

* Until 630 PM MDT.

* At 340 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Up to 1.75 inches of rain have
fallen. Additional rainfall amounts up to 0.5 inches are possible
in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Hueco Tanks and Hueco Mountain Estates.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 29 at 12:51PM HST until October 29 at 2:45PM HST by NWS Honolulu HI
properties.description:
At 1251 PM HST, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain over windward
Maui. Rain rates have decreased from earlier but is still falling at
a rate of 0.5 to 1.0 inch per hour. The heaviest rain is now over the
far eastern end of Maui near Hamoa and Kipahulu. Flash flooding is
ongoing. Additional bands of moderate to heavy rain will continue
over the next few hours.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by heavy rain.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Keanae, Nahiku, Kipahulu, Kaupo, Huelo, Makawao, Hana, Pukalani,
Haiku-Pauwela and Haliimaile.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 28 at 6:40PM MDT until October 29 at 6:45PM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is occurring.

* WHERE...South Central Socorro County in central New Mexico...

* WHEN...Until 645 PM MDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 638 PM MDT, emergency management reported flooding in the
warned area. Flooding is already occurring.
- Flooding was reported in Socorro County in the Escondida and
Pueblito Communities. Several roads have been rendered impassible
near San Pedro.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Socorro, San Antonio, Bosque Del Apache Refuge, Escondida,
Lemitar, San Acacia, Laborcita, Luis Lopez and Chamizal.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:

deaths occur in vehicles.
